entries.name: !crag.delay
entries.summary: Circular delay-line type
entries.body:
Represents an N-channel circular audio delay line.  `delaySize` is the
stated delay reading depth in samples per channel — the amount of audio
time that a `crag.pop_delay` or `crag.peek_delay` nominally reads back.
This is the value used by periodicity analysis and run-time estimates.

The optional `maxSize` parameter specifies the actual allocated buffer
size in samples per channel.  When `maxSize` is non-zero it must be
≥ `delaySize`; the buffer holds `maxSize` samples and `crag.peek_delay`
may read at offsets up to `maxSize` samples back.  This is useful for
modulated-delay effects (vibrato, chorus, flanger) where the read
position is swept by an LFO and needs headroom beyond the nominal delay.
When `maxSize` is 0 (the default) the buffer size equals `delaySize`.

Use `crag.delay_line` to obtain a handle, then `crag.push_delay` and
`crag.pop_delay` (or `crag.pop_delay_mix_in`) to write and read audio
blocks.  For modulated reads use `crag.peek_delay` with a runtime offset.

Examples:
```mlir
// Fixed 8192-sample delay — buffer and reading depth are both 8192.
%d = crag.delay_line : !crag.delay<f32, 48000, 1, 8192>

// Modulated delay: 960-sample nominal depth, 2400-sample buffer.
// peek_delay may read up to 2400 samples back; periodicity/runtime
// estimates use the 960-sample reading depth.
%d = crag.delay_line : !crag.delay<f32, 48000, 1, 960, 2400>
```

#### Parameters:

| Parameter | C++ type | Description |
| :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
| elemType | `::mlir::Type` |  |
| sampleRate | `unsigned` |  |
| channels | `unsigned` |  |
| delaySize | `unsigned` |  |
| maxSize | `unsigned` |  |

entries.name: !crag.freq_delay
entries.summary: Circular ring buffer of frequency-domain blocks
entries.body:
Syntax:

```
!crag.freq_delay<
  ::mlir::Type,   # elemType
  unsigned,   # sampleRate
  unsigned,   # channels
  unsigned   # numPartitions
>
```

A circular ring buffer that holds `numPartitions` frequency-domain blocks,
each produced by a `blockSize`-point real-to-complex FFT of an audio
signal.  Used as the persistent input-history store for partitioned
overlap-save FFT convolution.

Each slot holds `(blockSize/2 + 1) * channels` complex bins.  The
underlying storage is a flat `f32` global with real and imaginary parts
interleaved: slot `k` occupies positions
`[k*2*bins, (k+1)*2*bins - 1]` where `bins = (blockSize/2+1)*channels`.

Use `crag.freq_delay_line` to obtain a handle, `crag.push_freq_delay`
to insert a new block at the head (advancing the head pointer),
`crag.pop_freq_delay` to read the oldest block without advancing, and
`crag.peek_freq_delay` to read any block by partition index without
advancing.

Example:
```mlir
%fd = crag.freq_delay_line : !crag.freq_delay<f32, 48000, 1, 16>
crag.push_freq_delay %fd, %freq_block
    : !crag.freq_delay<f32, 48000, 1, 16>, !crag.freq<f32, 48000, 1>
%part0 = crag.peek_freq_delay %fd, %c0
    : !crag.freq_delay<f32, 48000, 1, 16>, i32 -> !crag.freq<f32, 48000, 1>
```

#### Parameters:

| Parameter | C++ type | Description |
| :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
| elemType | `::mlir::Type` |  |
| sampleRate | `unsigned` |  |
| channels | `unsigned` |  |
| numPartitions | `unsigned` |  |

entries.name: !crag.freq
entries.summary: Frequency-domain audio signal type
entries.body:
Syntax:

```
!crag.freq<
  ::mlir::Type,   # elemType
  unsigned,   # sampleRate
  unsigned   # channels
>
```

Represents the frequency-domain version of a `!crag.audio` signal,
produced by applying a real-to-complex FFT to an audio block.  Each
channel contributes `blockSize/2 + 1` complex bins, so the underlying
lowered tensor shape is `[(blockSize/2 + 1) * channels]` with element
type `complex<f32>`.

Use `crag.fft` to convert a `!crag.audio` block into a `!crag.freq`
block, `crag.ifft` to invert the transform, and `crag.freq_mul` to
multiply two frequency-domain blocks element-wise (complex multiply),
which is the core operation of FFT-based convolution.

The placeholder `!crag.freq<f32, 0, 0>` can be used inside named
subgraphs; the `crag-resolve-audio-rates` pass will fill in the actual
`sampleRate` and `channels` from the enclosing `crag.graph` attributes,
exactly as it does for `!crag.audio<f32, 0, 0>`.

Example:
```mlir
crag.graph sample_rate = 48000 channels = 1 {
  %noise    = crag.white_noise : !crag.audio<f32, 48000, 1>
  %freq     = crag.fft  %noise    : !crag.audio<f32, 48000, 1> -> !crag.freq<f32, 48000, 1>
  %filtered = crag.ifft %freq     : !crag.freq<f32, 48000, 1>  -> !crag.audio<f32, 48000, 1>
  crag.output %filtered : !crag.audio<f32, 48000, 1>
}
```

#### Parameters:

| Parameter | C++ type | Description |
| :-------: | :-------: | ----------- |
| elemType | `::mlir::Type` |  |
| sampleRate | `unsigned` |  |
| channels | `unsigned` |  |

entries.name: crag-canonicalize-primary-inputs
entries.summary: Rewrites top-level audio block-arguments into named crag.audio_input ops
entries.body:
Normalises how the unnamed (top-level) `crag.graph` declares its audio
inputs.  Two authoring styles are accepted:

1. Block-argument form (the historical style):
   ```mlir
   crag.graph sample_rate = 48000 channels = 1 {
   ^bb0(%in: !crag.audio<f32, 48000, 1>):
     crag.output %in : !crag.audio<f32, 48000, 1>
   }
   ```
2. Op-handle form (the canonical style introduced together with this pass):
   ```mlir
   crag.graph sample_rate = 48000 channels = 1 {
     %in = crag.audio_input "in" : !crag.audio<f32, 48000, 1>
     crag.output %in : !crag.audio<f32, 48000, 1>
   }
   ```

This pass converts any block-argument form on the unnamed graph into the
op-handle form so that all downstream passes (lowering, public-API
generation, instancing, optimisation passes, …) can assume a single
canonical representation.  Block-arguments are rewritten into
`crag.audio_input` ops with auto-generated names `input0`, `input1`, … in
block-argument order; original uses are RAUW-ed and the block-arguments
are erased.

Named library `crag.graph` subgraphs are left untouched: `crag.audio_input`
is illegal there, and they continue to declare their inputs as
block-arguments (which `crag-inline-subgraphs` later wires up).

The pass also records the canonical name<->index mapping on the unnamed
graph as a `crag.audio_input_names` `ArrayAttr` of `StringAttr`s so that
later passes (notably `crag-lower-audio-to-tensor` and
`crag-generate-public-api`) can recover the slot order without re-walking
the body.

The pass is idempotent: graphs that are already in op-handle form are
left structurally unchanged (only the `crag.audio_input_names` attribute
is freshened to reflect the body).

Pipeline placement: in the default `crag-compile` pipeline this pass runs
in Phase 1 immediately after `crag-inline-subgraphs`, so Phase 2 always
sees the canonical op-handle form.  Standalone use through `crag-opt`
remains valid for hand-authored block-argument inputs.

entries.name: crag-inline-funcs
entries.summary: Inlines named crag.func bodies referenced by crag.func_ref
entries.body:
Processes all `crag.func` ops in the module:
1. Detects reference cycles among `crag.func` ops (via nested
   `crag.func_ref` calls) and reports them as compile failures.
2. Flattens each `crag.func` body in topological order, inlining any
   nested `crag.func_ref` calls so that every `crag.func` becomes a
   single-level, `func_ref`-free body.
3. Inlines all remaining `crag.func_ref` ops in `crag.graph` and
   `crag.visualizer` bodies, substituting block arguments with the
   actual operands and replacing call results with the return values.
4. Erases all `crag.func` ops from the module.

This pass should run after `crag-resolve-includes` (which imports
`crag.include_func` ops) and before `crag-inline-subgraphs`.

entries.name: crag-inline-subgraphs
entries.summary: Inlines named crag.graph subgraphs referenced by crag.subgraph_ref
entries.body:
Detects reference cycles among named crag.graphs and treats any cycle as a
compile failure.  Then, for every crag.subgraph_ref op in the module,
clones the body of the referenced named graph directly into the caller at
the call site, substituting block arguments with the actual input operands.
After all references are inlined the named (subgraph) crag.graph ops are
removed from the module, leaving exactly one unnamed top-level graph ready
for subsequent lowering passes.

entries.name: crag-resolve-includes
entries.summary: Resolves crag.include ops by loading and merging external crag.mlir files
entries.body:
For every `crag.include` op in the module this pass:

1. Resolves the `path` attribute against the `include-dir` option
   (if set) or the current working directory.
2. Parses the referenced file as an MLIR module.
3. Finds the anonymous `crag.graph` in that module (or the named
   subgraph if there is no anonymous one) and clones it into the
   current module under the name given by `graph_name`.
4. If the `params_ns` attribute is present on the `crag.include` op,
   renames every `crag.param` in the cloned graph by prepending
   `params_ns + "."` to its name.
5. Removes the `crag.include` op.

This pass should run before `crag-verify-graph` in the pipeline.

Example:
```
crag-opt --crag-resolve-includes='include-dir=/path/to/standard-graphs' input.mlir
```

#### Options

```
-include-dir : Base directory for resolving relative paths in crag.include ops
```

entries.name: crag-resolve-visualizer-includes
entries.summary: Resolves crag.include_visualizer ops by loading external .mlir files
entries.body:
For every `crag.include_visualizer` op in the module this pass loads the
referenced file, finds the `crag.visualizer` inside, clones it into the
current module under the given name, and removes the include op.

#### Options

```
-include-dir : Base directory for resolving relative paths
```

entries.name: crag-unroll-parallel
entries.summary: Unrolls crag.parallel ops with a constant line count
entries.body:
Fully unrolls and inlines every `crag.parallel` whose `count` operand is a
compile-time constant `index` (an `arith.constant`).  For a count of N the
body region is cloned N times: the line-index block argument is bound to a
constant `arith.constant i : index`, and each capture block argument is
bound to the i-th element of its capture tensor (materialised as a scalar
constant when the tensor is a constant, else via `tensor.extract`).  The N
cloned `crag.parallel_yield` values are summed with `crag.sum` and replace
the op's result.  Each clone gets its own independent per-op state, exactly
as if the lines had been hand-written.

`crag.parallel` ops with a non-constant count are left untouched for
`crag-lower-audio-to-tensor` to lower into an `scf.for` reduction.  Runs
after `crag-inline-subgraphs`/`crag-inline-funcs` (so captures defined in
library graphs are already present) and before `crag-lower-audio-to-tensor`.

entries.name: crag-annotate-determinism
entries.summary: Annotates crag.graph ops with determinism information
entries.body:
Inspects each `crag.graph` in the module and marks it as deterministic by
attaching the unit attribute `crag.is_deterministic` when the graph body
contains no `crag.param` ops.  A graph that has at least one `crag.param`
is publicly controllable and is therefore *not* deterministic; the
attribute is removed from such graphs.

This pass is intended to run *after* `crag-inline-subgraphs` so that
params contributed by inlined subgraphs are visible in the top-level
graph body.

The attribute can be used by downstream passes (e.g.
`crag-fold-periodic-subgraphs`) to quickly skip graphs that contain
runtime-controllable parameters.

entries.name: crag-annotate-finiteness
entries.summary: Attach `crag.finite = N` to ops whose audio output is provably zero past sample N
entries.body:
Analysis pass for lazy wavetable caching of finite subgraphs with
infrequent inputs.

Walks each `crag.graph` body in topological (IR) order and stamps every
audio-producing op with a `crag.finite = N : i64` attribute when it can
statically prove that the op's audio output is zero for all samples
`n ≥ N` (counting from the most recent triggering input).  These
annotations are pure metadata: the pass never mutates op operands,
types, or graph structure.

Finiteness rules implemented:

  * `crag.sample` reading `[start, end)` of a sampler with a
    compile-time `inlined_length` and constant `start` / `end` operands:
    `N = max(0, end - start)`.  When `end` equals `inlined_length` and
    `start = 0` the op effectively plays the whole asset once.
  * `crag.adsr` with constant `attack_ms`, `decay_ms`, `release_ms`:
    `N = ceil((attack_ms + decay_ms + release_ms) * sample_rate / 1000)`.
    Note that this counts the one-shot envelope from trigger to release
    end; sustain hold is not considered an extension because the op's
    output decays to zero after the release segment.
  * `crag.scale`, `crag.hard_clip`, `crag.tanh` (memoryless): inherits
    the input's finite length.
  * `crag.sum` (variadic), `crag.audio_mul`, `crag.pop_delay_mix_in`:
    `N = max` over input finite lengths.  An input with no `crag.finite`
    attribute is treated as infinite, which collapses the result to
    infinite (no annotation).
  * `crag.pop_delay` / `crag.peek_delay`: when the matching
    `crag.push_delay` writes a finite-length input `N_in` into a delay
    line of `delaySize` samples, the pop/peek output is finite with
    `N_pop = N_in + delaySize`.  Detected by walking the immediate uses
    of the delay-line value.
  * `crag.delay_line` itself produces the SSA delay-line handle, not
    audio, and is not stamped.

Ops whose output is not provably finite (free-running oscillators,
`crag.white_noise`, `crag.wavetable_osc`, `crag.filter` without a
statically-known stable pole-radius bound, samplers with dynamic
bounds, and any op not enumerated above) are left unannotated.  An
unannotated audio value is treated as infinite by downstream
consumers, which is the safe default for the lazy-cache fold.

These annotations are intended for consumption by
`crag-fold-infrequent-finite-subgraphs` (the transform pass), which
combines them with the `crag.infrequent_inputs` annotation produced by
`crag-annotate-infrequent-region` to decide whether a subgraph is
eligible for lazy wavetable caching.

Should be run after `crag-resolve-audio-rates` and `crag-inline-graphs`
so the pass sees the post-inlined SSA graph with concrete sample-rate
values on every audio type.  Standalone analysis: not required to be
in the production lowering pipeline.

entries.name: crag-annotate-infrequent-region
entries.summary: Attach `crag.infrequent_inputs` to ops whose only non-constant transitive inputs are `infrequent` params/events
entries.body:
Analysis pass for lazy wavetable caching of finite subgraphs whose only
non-constant inputs are `infrequent` params/events.

Walks each `crag.graph` body in topological (IR) order and runs a
forward dataflow on the SSA graph that classifies every value as one of
three states:

  * `Const`      — comes only from compile-time constants
    (`arith.constant`, `crag.sample_rate`, transitively).
  * `Infrequent` — comes from constants and at least one `crag.param*`
    / `crag.event_*` op carrying the `infrequent` UnitAttr.
  * `AudioRate`  — depends on a non-`infrequent` param/event, on a
    live source (`crag.curframe`, `crag.white_noise`, …) or on any op
    we don't recognize as deterministic.  This poisons all downstream
    values and prevents the lazy-cache fold.

Propagation rules per op:

  * No operands:
    - `arith.constant`, `crag.sample_rate` → `Const`
    - `crag.param*` / `crag.event_*` with `infrequent` → `Infrequent`
    - anything else (including non-`infrequent` params/events,
      `crag.curframe`, `crag.white_noise`, …) → `AudioRate`
  * Has operands: combine operand states with `Const < Infrequent <
    AudioRate`; the op's state is the maximum.

Every op whose final state is `Infrequent` (i.e. all of its operands
are `Const`-or-`Infrequent` and at least one transitive input is an
`infrequent` param/event) is stamped with the
`crag.infrequent_inputs = unit` attribute.  Values whose state is
`Const` are left untagged on purpose: those are handled by the
pre-existing periodic / determinism folders, which produce strictly
cheaper code than a lazy cache.

These annotations are pure metadata: the pass never mutates op
operands, types, or graph structure, and downstream passes that ignore
the attribute behave exactly as before.  The annotations are intended
for consumption by `crag-fold-infrequent-finite-subgraphs` (the
transform pass), which combines them with the `crag.finite = N`
annotation produced by
`crag-annotate-finiteness` to decide whether a subgraph is eligible
for lazy wavetable caching.

Should be run after `crag-inline-graphs` so that the propagation sees
the fully-flattened SSA graph.  Standalone analysis: not required to
be in the production lowering pipeline.

entries.name: crag-apply-adaa
entries.summary: Rewrites supported nonlinear audio ops to ADAA variants
entries.body:
Walks each `crag.graph` and identifies supported memoryless nonlinear audio
ops (`crag.tanh`, `crag.hard_clip`), then rewrites them to explicit ADAA
forms (`crag.adaa_tanh`, `crag.adaa_hard_clip`) unless `report-only=true`.

In report-only mode the pass emits diagnostics for candidate ops but leaves
IR unchanged.

#### Options

```
-mode        : ADAA quality mode (`first-order` for MVP; `second-order` reserved)
-epsilon     : Denominator threshold for stable ADAA fallback logic
-ops         : Comma-separated allowlist: `all`, `tanh`, `hard_clip`
-report-only : Emit ADAA candidate remarks without rewriting IR
```

entries.name: crag-build-multiview-visualizer
entries.summary: Combines PCM-compatible crag.visualizer ops into a single tiled multiview
entries.body:
Collects all `crag.visualizer` ops in the module that are compatible with
a shared PCM audio buffer (oscilloscope, loudness-meter, loudness-history,
and any visualizer using the new-viz-ops body style).  Visualizers that
require a different audio buffer format — spectrometer (FFT magnitudes),
phase-correlation (interleaved stereo), or compressor-viz (extra GR
argument) — are left untouched.

When two or more compatible visualizers are found the pass:

1. Computes a grid layout with `num-cols` columns.  Each tile has
   dimensions equal to the largest width and largest height across all
   compatible visualizers.
2. Creates a new `crag.visualizer` named "multiview" whose body:
   - Fills a black canvas of size `(cols * tileW) x (rows * tileH)`.
   - For each compatible visualizer at its fixed grid position (row, col),
     clones the visualizer's body ops (remapping the audio block argument)
     and overlays the resulting texture onto the canvas at pixel offset
     `(col * tileW, row * tileH)` using `crag.viz_overlay`.
   - Outputs the composite canvas.
3. Replaces every `crag.visualizer_ref` that referenced a compatible
   visualizer with a single `crag.visualizer_ref "multiview"` on the
   top-level graph's audio output.
4. Removes the now-inlined compatible `crag.visualizer` ops.

Each visualizer always occupies the same grid tile across process
callbacks because tile assignment is based on encounter order in the
module, which is fixed at compile time.

This pass must run after `crag-inject-visualizer` (or after any pass that
produces `crag.visualizer` ops) and before
`crag-lower-visualizer-to-tensor`.

#### Options

```
-num-cols : Number of columns in the multiview tile grid
```

entries.name: crag-fold-infrequent-finite-subgraphs
entries.summary: Replace finite subgraphs whose only non-constant inputs are `infrequent` with a `crag.lazy_wavetable` cache
entries.body:
Transform pass for lazy wavetable caching of finite subgraphs with
infrequent inputs.

Walks each top-level (unnamed) `crag.graph` and, for every audio-producing
op `R` that simultaneously carries
  * `crag.finite = N : i64` (from `crag-annotate-finiteness`) with
    `min-tail-samples ≤ N ≤ max-cache-samples`, and
  * `crag.infrequent_inputs = unit` (from
    `crag-annotate-infrequent-region`),
and whose audio result is not feeding *another* such candidate (i.e. `R`
is the maximal eligible boundary on its chain), the pass:

  1. Computes the producer closure of `R` within the graph body — every
     op transitively feeding `R` whose own state is `Const` or
     `Infrequent`.  The walk stops at any op that does not carry
     `crag.infrequent_inputs` and is not itself a recognized constant
     leaf (`arith.constant`, `crag.sample_rate`) or an `infrequent`
     param/event.
  2. Identifies the "captured infrequent inputs": the `crag.param*` and
     `crag.event_*` ops carrying `infrequent` reached during the walk.
     Their result values become the `inputs` operand list of the new
     `crag.lazy_wavetable`; for event ops, the `fired` result is also
     appended to the `triggers` operand list (so lowering can compute
     the dirty bit).
  3. Materialises a private `memref.global "private"
     @crag_lazycache_<id>_table : memref<N x f32> = dense<0.0>` at module
     scope to back the lazy cache.
  4. Materialises a private named `crag.graph @_crag_lazy_subgraph_<id>`
     at module scope holding a clone of the entire producer closure
     (including the captured infrequent param/event ops, so the
     subgraph is self-contained), with `crag.output` returning the
     cloned root's audio result.  This is the canonical record of what
     the thunk renders; the lowering pass consumes it to populate the
     body of the thunk function.
  5. Materialises a private
     `func.func private @_crag_lazy_render_<id>(args..., %table)`.
     For closures consisting of an inlined-sampler `crag.sample`
     (with constant `start`/`end`) followed by zero or more pointwise
     ops in `{crag.scale, crag.hard_clip, crag.tanh}` whose scalar
     arguments are either constants or captured `infrequent` inputs,
     the body is fully populated: the sliced PCM is materialised as a
     private `memref.global "private" constant
     @crag_lazycache_<id>_src`, and the body emits an `scf.for` that
     loads from it, applies the resolved pipeline (forwarding
     captured inputs as function args), and stores into `%table`.
     For unsupported closure shapes (e.g. ADSR roots, delay-line
     readers, `audio_mul` / `sum` combinators), the body falls back
     to a `return`-only stub; populating those is a lowering-pass
     follow-up.
  6. Replaces `R` in the parent graph with a single
     `crag.lazy_wavetable @crag_lazycache_<id>_table,
                           thunk = @_crag_lazy_render_<id>,
                           inputs = (...), triggers = (...),
                           length = N : (...) -> !crag.audio<...>`
     and erases `R` together with the now-dead producers in the
     parent graph that have no remaining users.

Eligibility hard-fails (the candidate is left untouched):
  * `R`'s audio result type is not single-channel `f32`
    (multi-channel handling is left to a future iteration).
  * The producer closure escapes the parent graph body (uses an
    unrecognized leaf, a block argument, or a value defined outside).
  * No infrequent param/event reachable from `R` (the fold would
    degenerate to a periodic case already handled by
    `crag-fold-periodic-subgraphs`).
  * `N < min-tail-samples` or `N > max-cache-samples`.

Pass placement: after `crag-resolve-audio-rates`, `crag-inline-graphs`,
`crag-annotate-periodicity`, `crag-fold-periodic-subgraphs`,
`crag-annotate-finiteness`, and `crag-annotate-infrequent-region`;
before `crag-lower-audio-to-tensor`.  Periodic folding must run first
so that periodic interiors of a finite tail are caught as cheaper
`crag.wavetable_osc` ops before they would be wrapped in a lazy cache.

#### Options

```
-max-cache-samples : Maximum per-channel cache size in samples (default 1<<20, ~22 s @ 48 kHz).  Subgraphs with `crag.finite = N` larger than this are not folded
-min-tail-samples  : Minimum per-channel cache size in samples below which the cache overhead exceeds the saved DSP cost; smaller subgraphs are skipped
```

entries.name: crag-fold-periodic-subgraphs
entries.summary: Replaces provably periodic oscillators with pre-computed wave table lookups
entries.body:
Analyzes each `crag.graph` body and replaces oscillator ops
(`crag.sine`, `crag.saw`, `crag.square`, `crag.tri`) whose `freq`,
`phase`, and `duty` inputs are all compile-time constants with
`crag.wavetable_osc` ops that read from a pre-computed in-memory wave
table.

**Periodicity detection**

An oscillator whose inputs are all constants is provably periodic with
period `P = round(sample_rate / freq)` samples.  The pass also inspects
downstream `crag.filter` and `crag.delay_line` chains: a stable IIR
filter fed by a periodic signal eventually produces a periodic output
with the same period; a delay line with no feedback on a periodic input
also becomes periodic once the stated reading depth (`delaySize`
samples) of the periodic signal has been pushed into the buffer.
For modulated delays with a larger backing buffer (`maxSize >
delaySize`), the relevant fill depth for periodicity analysis is still
the nominal `delaySize` reading depth, not the full buffer.  These
chains are annotated but not yet folded in this release.

**Wave table generation**

For each eligible oscillator the pass:
1. Computes `period = round(sample_rate / freq)`.  If `period` exceeds
   `max-fold-period` the oscillator is skipped entirely.
2. Pre-evaluates the waveform for all `period` samples using the same
   formulas as the corresponding lowering pass.
3. Recursively folds the computed table to its minimum exact sub-period
   `P'`: the smallest divisor `P'` of `period` such that
   `table[i] == table[i % P']` for every `i` in `[0, period)`.
   If `P'` exceeds `max-table-samples` the oscillator is not stored.
4. Stores the (possibly reduced) table as a private `memref.global`
   constant named `@crag_wavetable_N_data` (N = sequential index) with
   size `P'`.
5. Replaces the oscillator op with a `crag.wavetable_osc` op that
   references the global and carries `P'` as the `period` attribute.

**Recursive wavetable folding (correctness)**

The sub-period reduction is provably exact.  The `WaveTableOscOp`
lowering reads `out[k] = table[(curframe + k) % period]`.  If `P'`
divides `period` and `table[j] == table[j % P']` for all `j < period`,
then for any `curframe` and `k`:

  `(curframe + k) % period` takes a value `j` in `[0, period)`, and
  `j % P' == (curframe + k) % P'` (because `P'` divides `period`).

Therefore `table[(curframe + k) % period] == table[(curframe + k) % P']`
exactly, so replacing `period` with `P'` produces bit-identical audio.

**Lowering**

`CragLowerAudioToTensor` handles `crag.wavetable_osc` by generating a
`scf.for` loop that reads from the wave table global at index
`(curframe + i) % period` for each sample position `i` in the block.
This is numerically equivalent to the original oscillator formula when
`period * freq == sample_rate` exactly (i.e. the frequency divides the
sample rate).  For non-integer periods the maximum per-block phase error
is `|freq / sample_rate|` radians, which is inaudible in practice.

**Eligibility**

An oscillator is eligible for folding when:
- All input values are compile-time constants (derived solely from
  `arith.constant` or `crag.sample_rate`, possibly through `arith`
  arithmetic ops).
- `freq > 0`.
- The computed period does not exceed `max-fold-period`.
- After recursive sub-period reduction, the stored period does not
  exceed `max-table-samples`.

**Wave-player asset pre-analysis**

For each `crag.sample` op whose source `crag.sampler` carries an
`inlined_data` attribute (compile-time-embedded PCM byte array) and
whose `start` / `end` arguments match the wave-player loop pattern
(`end == N`, `start ≡ curframe (mod N)`, where `N` is the inlined data
length), the pass replaces the sample op with a `crag.wavetable_osc`
that reads from a private `memref.global` constant containing the
asset's PCM (after recursive sub-period reduction via the same
`findMinSubperiod` logic used for oscillator folding).  This sweep
runs before periodicity analysis so that any downstream chain
(`scale`, `filter`, `sum`, …) feeding off the new `crag.wavetable_osc`
can in turn be absorbed by the periodic subgraph and multi-oscillator
folding sweeps.  Restricted to single-channel output and `f32` inlined
data.

This pass requires `crag-resolve-audio-rates` to have run first (so that
audio types carry concrete sample-rate values).  It should run before
`crag-lower-audio-to-tensor`.

#### Options

```
-max-table-samples     : Maximum wave table size in samples for the stored (possibly folded) wavetable; oscillators whose minimum sub-period exceeds this limit are not folded
-max-fold-period       : Maximum oscillator period in samples to attempt folding; oscillators with a longer period are skipped even if their minimum sub-period would fit within max-table-samples.  Set this higher than max-table-samples to enable recursive folding of large periods into compact sub-period tables
-max-transient-samples : Maximum allowed transient length (in samples) for a periodic-subgraph fold.  Folding requires simulating `transient + period` samples of the chain, so very long transients (e.g. a delay-line of millions of samples) are rejected to keep compile time bounded.  Has no effect on bare oscillators (transient = 0)
-max-lcm-period        : Maximum combined period (in samples) for folding a multi-oscillator junction (`crag.sum` or `crag.audio_mul`) whose output period was widened by an `lcm` across inputs of differing individual periods.  When the junction's `lcm` exceeds this limit, the junction itself is left intact and each input chain is folded independently into its own wavetable.  Junctions whose inputs all share the same period (so `lcm` did not widen) are gated by `max-fold-period` only.  This option is independent of `max-fold-period` because `lcm` can grow much faster than any individual oscillator period
```

entries.name: crag-inject-channel-mixers
entries.summary: Injects channel-count conversion graphs around graph I/O
entries.body:
Walks the unnamed top-level `crag.graph` and injects standard-graph
channel-mixing subgraphs at every channel-count boundary:

* **Output side.**  When the graph's `channels` attribute differs from
  `target-channels`, the named mixer's body is inlined immediately
  before the `crag.output` op and the graph's `channels` attribute is
  updated to `target-channels`.  Skipped when `target-channels` is 0.
* **Input side.**  For every `crag.audio_input` op whose result-type
  channel count is non-zero and differs from the graph's `channels`
  attribute, the matching mixer is inlined immediately *after* the
  input op and all downstream uses are rewired through the mixed
  signal.  This lets a graph accept host-supplied audio at one
  channel count and process it internally at another.  Always runs;
  a no-op when no input has a mismatch.

Mixer-name precedence:

1. The per-target attribute (`crag.audio_input`'s
   `preferred_channel_mixer` for input-side; `crag.graph`'s
   `preferred_channel_mixer` for output-side).
2. The `mixer-name` pass option.
3. A built-in default derived from the source→target channel counts
   (e.g. `"stereo_to_mono_average"` for 2→1).

Valid built-in mixer names are:
* `"mono_to_stereo"`            — duplicate mono to L and R channels
* `"stereo_to_mono_average"`    — (L + R) / 2  (FLAT ITU downmix)
* `"stereo_to_mono_left"`       — left channel only
* `"stereo_to_mono_right"`      — right channel only
* `"stereo_to_mono_mid_side"`   — mid = (L + R) / 2  (same as average,
                                   but named for M/S processing context)
* `"stereo_to_51"`              — stereo to 5.1 phantom-centre upmix
* `"51_to_stereo"`              — 5.1 → stereo ITU-R BS.775 downmix

The pass loads each standard-graph file from `include-dir` (if
supplied) or from the same directory as the input file.

Pipeline placement: after `crag-resolve-audio-rates`, before
`crag-lower-audio-to-tensor`.  Safe to invoke unconditionally — the
pass is a no-op when no boundaries need conversion.

#### Options

```
-target-channels : Desired output channel count (0 = skip output-side injection)
-mixer-name      : Name of the standard-graph channel mixer to inject
-include-dir     : Base directory for loading standard-graph mixer files
```

entries.name: crag-inject-output-meters
entries.summary: Injects a crag.meter on the output of each named subgraph
entries.body:
For every named `crag.graph` subgraph in the module, this pass:

1. Computes the peak absolute sample level of the graph's audio output
   using `crag.audio_peak`.
2. Posts it to a `crag.meter` named after the graph (e.g. "reverb"),
   with `min = 0.0` and `max = 1.0`.

This pass must run after `crag-resolve-includes` and before
`crag-inline-subgraphs` so that named subgraph boundaries are visible.

It is used by `crag-compile --inject-output-meters` to automatically
instrument every subgraph output with a level meter for monitoring.

entries.name: crag-inject-visualizer
entries.summary: Injects a crag.visualizer_ref on the final output of the compiled graph
entries.body:
Inserts a `crag.visualizer_ref "<viz-name>"(%output_audio)` immediately
before the `crag.output` op of the top-level unnamed `crag.graph`.  The
named visualizer must already exist in the module (import it with
`crag.include_visualizer` first, or inject via `--inject-visualizer` in
`crag-compile`).

This pass also imports the named visualizer from the standard-graphs
directory when the `visualizer-type` option is `"oscilloscope"`,
`"spectrometer"`, `"phase-correlation"`, `"loudness-meter"`,
`"loudness-history"`, or `"compressor-viz"`.

#### Options

```
-viz-name    : Name of the crag.visualizer to inject
-viz-type    : Built-in visualizer type to create: oscilloscope, spectrometer, phase-correlation, loudness-meter, loudness-history, or compressor-viz
-viz-width   : Visualizer image width in pixels
-viz-height  : Visualizer image height in pixels
-include-dir : Base directory for loading the standard-graphs visualizer file
```

entries.name: crag-resolve-audio-rates
entries.summary: Resolves placeholder 0/0 sample_rate and channels in crag.graph and !crag.audio types
entries.body:
Fills in zero-valued sample_rate and channels placeholders:

* Any `crag.graph` with `sample_rate=0` has that value replaced by the
  `sample-rate` pass option (if non-zero).
* Any `crag.graph` with `channels=0` has that value replaced by the
  `channels` pass option (if non-zero).
* Any `!crag.audio<elemType, 0, 0>` type inside a `crag.graph` is
  updated to `!crag.audio<elemType, SR, CH>` where SR and CH are the
  resolved sample_rate and channels of the enclosing graph.

This pass should run after `crag-inline-subgraphs` in the pipeline, and
before any lowering pass that reads sample_rate or channels from audio
types (e.g. `crag-lower-audio-to-tensor`).

In test files, write `!crag.audio<f32, 0, 0>` as a placeholder; the pass
will fill in the values from the enclosing `crag.graph` attributes.  If
the graph itself uses `sample_rate=0 channels=0`, supply the desired
values via the `sample-rate` and `channels` options (e.g. from the
compile stage).

#### Options

```
-sample-rate : Sample rate to assign to crag.graph ops whose sample_rate=0
-channels    : Channel count to assign to crag.graph ops whose channels=0
```

entries.name: crag-resolve-channel-counts
entries.summary: Resolves channel count placeholders (0) in crag types
entries.body:
Fills in a channel count of `0` in `!crag.audio`, `!crag.freq`, and
`!crag.delay` types that appear inside `crag.graph` ops, using the
enclosing graph's `channels` attribute as the concrete value.

A channel count of `0` is the conventional placeholder meaning
"inherit from the enclosing graph".  Unlike `crag-resolve-audio-rates`
(which handles both sample rate and channel count simultaneously), this
pass focuses exclusively on channel counts and — critically — also
handles `!crag.delay` types, which `crag-resolve-audio-rates` does not
update.

When the `channels` pass option is provided (non-zero) and a graph
carries a `channels = 0` attribute, the graph attribute itself is first
updated before the body types are resolved.

This pass should run after `crag-resolve-audio-rates` in the pipeline
(or independently when only channel resolution is needed).

Example:
```
crag-opt --crag-resolve-channel-counts='channels=2' input.mlir
```

#### Options

```
-channels : Channel count override (0 = read from graph attribute)
```

entries.name: crag-resolve-delay-timings
entries.summary: Resolves duration-based delay timings to sample counts
entries.body:
Converts `crag.delay_line` duration timing attributes (`delay_timing`,
`max_timing`) into concrete `!crag.delay` sample-count fields.

For each `crag.delay_line` carrying
`delay_timing = !crag.duration<U>` (microseconds):
  * `delaySize` becomes `round((U / 1_000_000) * sample_rate)`.
If `max_timing` is present:
  * `maxSize` becomes `round((Umax / 1_000_000) * sample_rate)`.

The pass updates the delay-line result type and all delay-handle user
operand types (`push_delay`, `pop_delay`, `pop_delay_mix_in`,
`peek_delay`) to keep IR type-consistent, then removes timing attributes.

Sample rate resolution for conversion:
  1. Delay type sampleRate when non-zero.
  2. Enclosing `crag.graph` sample_rate when non-zero.
  3. `sample-rate` pass option when non-zero.

This pass should run before any pass that consumes delay sample counts
(`crag-infer-delay-sizes`, periodicity/tail analysis, and lowering).

#### Options

```
-sample-rate : Sample-rate fallback when delay and graph sample rates are 0
```

entries.name: crag-resolve-preferred-resampler
entries.summary: Resolves and propagates preferred_resampler attributes on crag.graph and crag.sampler ops
entries.body:
Ensures each `crag.graph` and `crag.sampler` op carries a valid
`preferred_resampler` attribute by following a fallback chain:

1. The op's own `preferred_resampler` attribute (if present and non-empty).
2. For `crag.sampler`: the enclosing `crag.graph`'s resolved value.
3. The `default-resampler` pass option (set by `crag-compile`).
4. The built-in default: `"bandlimited_sinc"`.

Valid resampler names are:
* `"lagrangian"`       — 4-point cubic Lagrange block interpolation
* `"thiran"`           — Thiran allpass-chain fractional delay
* `"bandlimited_sinc"` — windowed-sinc anti-alias + allpass diffuser

An error is emitted for any unknown name found on an op or provided as
the default.  This pass is intended to run after `crag-inline-subgraphs`
and before any lowering pass.

#### Options

```
-default-resampler : Default preferred resampler when none is specified on the graph or sampler
```

entries.name: crag-verify-graph
entries.summary: Verifies structural constraints of crag.graph IR

entries.name: crag-build-state-struct
entries.summary: Emits the per-instance state-struct lifecycle ABI (size, init, create, destroy, count, handle, id-from-handle)
entries.body:
Reads the `crag.state_layout` module attribute (produced by
`crag-collect-state-layout`) and emits the per-instance state-struct
lifecycle entry points:

* `@crag_instance_state_size() -> i64` — returns the byte size of
  the `%CragInstanceState` struct (matches `crag.state_struct_bytes`).
* `@_crag_init_instance(!llvm.ptr) -> ()` — extension point for
  per-field initialisation.  In PR 0-B this is an empty no-op stub:
  `crag_instance_create` allocates with `@calloc`, which already
  zero-fills the buffer, so no extra work is required.  PR 0-C will
  extend this body with the per-field non-zero default-value writes
  (e.g. seeding `crag_filter_state_*` with the documented default
  coefficients) once `CragInstantiateGlobals` has rerouted reads
  through the struct.
* `@crag_instance_create() -> i32` — `@calloc(1, state_size)`,
  stores the returned pointer in the in-`.so` instance table,
  returns the 1-based id, or 0 on failure.
* `@crag_instance_destroy(i32 id)` — `@free`s the pointer in slot
  `id - 1` and clears the slot.
* `@crag_instance_count() -> i32` — returns the live count.
* `@crag_instance_handle(i32 id) -> !llvm.ptr` — returns the raw
  state pointer for `id`, or null if `id` is out of range / unused.
* `@crag_instance_id_from_handle(!llvm.ptr) -> i32` — linear scan
  of the table; returns the matching 1-based id or 0 if not found.

Backing storage:

* `@crag_inst_table : memref<256xi64>` — slot `i` holds the raw
  state pointer (cast to i64) for instance id `i + 1`, or 0 if free.
  Capping at 256 instances per `.so` is intentional in PR 0-B; the
  cache will own a dynamically-sized table once PR 0-D lands and
  `--no-instance-table` becomes meaningful.
* `@crag_inst_count : memref<1xi32>` — current live count.

The table is **not** thread-safe in PR 0-B (concurrent
`_create` / `_destroy` calls race).  This is acceptable because the
only consumers are single-threaded test hosts; the cache (which
needs concurrency) lands in PR 0-D and brings its own table.

Gated on `emit-instancing` upstream — this pass is unconditional
once added to the pipeline, but the upstream pipeline only adds it
when `CragCompileOptions::emitInstancing` is true.

entries.name: crag-collect-state-layout
entries.summary: Records the per-instance state layout as a module attribute
entries.body:
Walks every mutable, non-constant `memref.global` in the module that is
part of the per-instance state of a compiled crag graph and records an
ordered description of the fields as the `crag.state_layout` module
attribute (an `ArrayAttr` of `DictionaryAttr`s with `name`, `bytes`,
and `offset` keys).  Also records the total in-bytes on the module as
`crag.state_struct_bytes : i64`.

A global is considered per-instance state unless it is read-only
(constant), is a visualizer canvas output (`crag_viz_output` — a
shared multi-view tile buffer, not per-instance), or is the
lifecycle backing global itself (`crag_inst_table` /
`crag_inst_count`).  Read-only constants such as sampler-name byte
arrays, inlined PCM, and folded-wavetable PCM are already excluded
by the `getConstant()` filter.  `crag_output` IS included so the
runtime `crag_instance_state_size()` agrees with `.cragmeta`'s
`instance_memory.state_struct_bytes` from PR 0-A; PR 0-C will keep
the legacy `crag_output` module symbol alive as a shim that points
at the default instance's output field.

Field offsets use natural alignment to the field's element size
(bumped to 8 bytes for any field whose element size is < 8 — i.e. the
final layout is conservatively i64-aligned).  This matches the
`state_struct_bytes` total reported by `.cragmeta`'s
`instance_memory` block (which sums element-bytes without padding;
the layout pass uses the larger, padded total for runtime
allocation).

This pass is the canonical source of truth for the instance state
layout — every downstream pass that walks per-instance state must
consume `crag.state_layout` rather than re-discover globals
independently.

entries.name: crag-generate-public-api
entries.summary: Generates C-compatible public API functions for a compiled crag graph
entries.body:
After `crag-lower-audio-to-tensor` (with use-global-params=true), adds:

* `@crag_output : memref<blockSizexf32>` — public output buffer
* `@crag_process()` — runs the graph, writes result to `@crag_output`
* `@crag_set_param(i32, f32)` — sets parameter by index
* `@crag_get_param(i32) -> f32` — reads parameter by index
* `@crag_num_params() -> i32` — returns number of parameters
* `@crag_sample_rate() -> i32` — returns sample rate constant
* `@crag_num_channels() -> i32` — returns channel count constant
* `@crag_block_size() -> i32` — returns block size constant

These functions have C-compatible calling conventions and are exported
as shared library entry points when compiled to a `.so`/`.dll`.

entries.name: crag-generate-visualizer-api
entries.summary: Generates public C API functions for the crag.visualizer
entries.body:
After `crag-lower-visualizer-to-tensor`, adds:

* `@crag_num_visualizers() -> i32` — number of visualizers in the module
* `@crag_has_visualizer() -> i32`  — 1 if any visualizer is present
* `@crag_visualize(i32)`           — runs visualizer idx on captured audio,
                                     writes RGBA pixels to @crag_viz_output
* `@crag_viz_output : memref<WxHx4xf32>` — public RGBA output buffer
* `@crag_viz_width(i32) -> i32`    — image width for visualizer idx
* `@crag_viz_height(i32) -> i32`   — image height for visualizer idx

entries.name: crag-instantiate-globals
entries.summary: Threads a per-instance state pointer through @crag_graph and the singleton-shim entry points (PR 0-C-1 skeleton)
entries.body:
PR 0-C-1 skeleton.

This pass runs after `crag-build-state-struct` (gated upstream on
`CragCompileOptions::emitInstancing`) and before `crag-bufferize`.  In
PR 0-C-1 it is a *skeleton*: it sets up the calling-convention surface
that subsequent sub-PRs (0-C-2 .. 0-C-6) will use, but it does **not**
rewrite any `memref::GetGlobalOp` site yet.

What lands in 0-C-1:

* Adds a leading `!llvm.ptr` argument named `%inst_state` to
  `@crag_graph`.  The argument is currently unused inside the graph
  body — sub-PRs 0-C-2 .. 0-C-6 will incrementally GEP into it to
  replace per-instance `memref::GetGlobalOp` reads.  All existing
  callers of `@crag_graph` (in PR 0-B that is just `@crag_process`)
  are updated to forward the pointer.

* Emits the singleton-shim helpers:
    - `@_crag_default_id : memref<1xi32>` (initialised to 0).
    - `@crag_default_instance() -> i32` — lazily calls
      `@crag_instance_create()` on the first invocation and caches the
      1-based id in `@_crag_default_id`.  PR 0-B's `_crag_init_instance`
      stub is the callee through `crag_instance_create`, so this just
      works.

* Updates `@crag_process` to call `crag_default_instance()` →
  `crag_instance_handle()` and forward the resulting `!llvm.ptr` to
  `@crag_graph`.  Other public-API entry points (`crag_set_param`,
  `crag_get_meter`, etc.) are NOT touched in 0-C-1; they continue to
  read/write the module-scope globals exactly as today.  They will be
  converted family-by-family in 0-C-2 .. 0-C-6 as their backing
  globals get GEP'd into the state struct.

* Reads `crag.state_layout` and runs a debug-only audit
  (`-debug-only=crag-instantiate-globals`) that lists every
  `memref::GetGlobalOp` whose target appears in the layout.  In
  PR 0-C-1 every site is, by definition, unrewritten — the audit is
  informational and never fails.  Sub-PR 0-C-6 tightens this into a
  hard failure once the rewrite engine is complete.

Default path (`emitInstancing=false`): this pass is not added to the
pipeline, so the generated `.so` is bit-identical to today.

entries.name: crag-lower-audio-to-tensor
entries.summary: Lowers crag.audio types to tensors and crag ops to linalg/tensor ops
entries.body:
Replaces all `!crag.audio<...>` types with `tensor<N x f32>` (where N =
block_size * channels) and converts each crag op inside a `crag.graph` to
an equivalent standard-dialect op.

Default mode (inline-runtime-functions=false):
* `crag.param`                  → `arith.constant` (default value)
* `crag.white_noise`            → `linalg.fill` into `tensor.empty`
* `crag.get_filter_coeffs`      → `func.call` to runtime helper
* `crag.filter`                 → `func.call` to runtime helper
* `crag.are_filter_coeffs_stable` → `func.call` to runtime helper

Compile mode (inline-runtime-functions=true, use-global-params=true):
* `crag.param`      → `memref.load` from global `@crag_params` table
* `crag.white_noise`→ inline LCG loop with per-instance global state
* `crag.get_filter_coeffs` → inline Butterworth coefficient computation
                              using `math.tan` + `arith.*` + `tensor.*`
* `crag.filter`     → inline IIR filter loop with per-instance global state
* `crag.are_filter_coeffs_stable` → inline stability check

In both modes:
* `crag.graph`      → `func.func`
* `crag.sample_rate`→ `arith.constant`
* `crag.sum`        → chain of `linalg.add`
* `crag.output`     → `func.return`

#### Options

```
-block-size               : Number of audio samples per block in the lowered tensor shape
-inline-runtime-functions : Inline filter/noise implementations using MLIR math/scf ops
-use-global-params        : Lower crag.param to reads from a global @crag_params memref
-strict-bounds-checks     : Insert runtime bounds checks on every parameter-/runtime-driven buffer access (peek_delay offset, peek_freq_delay partition_idx, crag.sample start).  On the first violation the generated code calls __crag_bounds_fail, which prints a structured report (graph source location, op, idx, buf size) and aborts.
```

entries.name: crag-lower-visualizer-to-tensor
entries.summary: Lowers crag.visualizer bodies and crag.visualizer_ref ops to tensor/func IR
entries.body:
Compiles every `crag.visualizer` op in the module:
- Lowers `crag.waveform` to a `scf.for` loop over pixel columns that reads
  audio samples and sets RGBA pixels on the waveform trace.
- Lowers `crag.fft` + `crag.spectrogram` to an FFT capture + bar-chart
  renderer.  At capture time the pass calls `crag_rt_fft` on the audio
  tensor and stores the per-bin magnitudes (channel 0, normalised to
  [0, 1]) into the `crag_viz_<name>_audio_buf` global.  The impl function
  renders a green bar chart from those pre-computed magnitudes.
- Lowers `crag.phase_corr` to a loop over sample pairs that plots each
  (left, right) pair as a green dot in a Lissajous figure.
- Lowers `crag.peak_meter` to a loop that finds the peak absolute sample
  value and renders a color-coded vertical bar (green / yellow / red).
- Emits a function `@crag_viz_<name>_impl(memref<Nxf32>, memref<WxHx4xf32>)`
  that implements the visualizer body.
- Lowers `crag.visualizer_ref "name"(%audio)` to:
  - For oscilloscope / phase-correlation / loudness-meter: stores the
    audio tensor into `@crag_viz_<name>_audio_buf`.
  - For spectrometer: calls `crag_rt_fft`, computes per-bin magnitudes,
    and stores them (normalised f32) into `@crag_viz_<name>_audio_buf`.
- Creates a global `@crag_viz_output` (RGBA pixel buffer).
- Creates a `@crag_viz_<name>_audio_buf` global for the captured data.
  For `crag.phase_corr` the buffer holds `blockSize * 2` samples
  (interleaved L/R).  For `crag.spectrogram` it holds `blockSize/2 + 1`
  f32 magnitude bins.  For all other ops it holds `blockSize` samples.

#### Options

```
-block-size           : Audio block size in samples
-strict-bounds-checks : Insert runtime bounds checks on parameter-driven texture / audio-buffer indices in visualizer rendering.  See the CragLowerAudioToTensor option of the same name for runtime behavior.
```

entries.name: crag-bufferize
entries.summary: Bufferizes tensor IR to memref IR using One-Shot Bufferize
entries.body:
Converts tensor-typed values produced by `crag-lower-audio-to-tensor` into
memref-typed values using MLIR's One-Shot Module Bufferize algorithm.

For each `func.func` in the module the pass:
* Converts `tensor.empty` to `memref.alloc`.
* Converts `linalg.fill` / `linalg.add` operating on tensors to their
  in-place memref equivalents.
* Updates `func.call` operand and result types from tensor to memref.
* Updates the function signature (arguments and return types) accordingly.

Any `bufferization.dealloc` operations inserted by the analysis are
immediately lowered to `memref.dealloc` before the pass completes.

This pass is intended to follow `crag-lower-audio-to-tensor` in the
compilation pipeline and to precede `crag-lower-to-llvm`.

entries.name: crag-lower-to-llvm
entries.summary: Lowers bufferized IR to the LLVM dialect
entries.body:
Drives a standard MLIR lowering pipeline that converts the output of
`crag-bufferize` (memref + linalg + arith + math + func + cf IR) all the
way to the LLVM dialect.

The pipeline applied is:
1. `tosa-to-linalg` / `tosa-to-linalg-named` — lowers any TOSA ops that
   may be present (enables TOSA-based producers upstream).
2. `convert-math-to-libm` — lowers `math.*` ops (tan, sqrt, …) to libm.
3. `convert-linalg-to-loops` — expands `linalg.fill` / `linalg.add` to
   `scf.for` loops.
4. `convert-scf-to-cf` — lowers SCF structured control flow to
   `cf.br` / `cf.cond_br`.
5. `finalize-memref-to-llvm` — converts `memref.*` ops to LLVM equivalents.
6. `arith-to-llvm` — converts `arith.*` arithmetic operations to LLVM.
7. `convert-func-to-llvm` — lowers `func.func` and `func.call` to LLVM.
8. `convert-cf-to-llvm` — lowers remaining `cf.*` ops to LLVM branches.
9. `reconcile-unrealized-casts` — eliminates leftover conversion casts.

After this pass the module contains only LLVM dialect ops and is ready for
translation to LLVM IR via `mlir-translate --mlir-to-llvmir`.

entries.name: crag-annotate-periodicity
entries.summary: Attach `crag.period` / `crag.transient` annotations to ops whose audio result is statically periodic
entries.body:
Walks each `crag.graph` body in topological order and attaches two
integer attributes to every op producing a `!crag.audio` result whose
output sequence can be proven periodic at compile time:

  * `crag.period`   = `i64`, the (possibly conservative) period in
    samples of the op's audio result.
  * `crag.transient` = `i64`, the number of leading output samples that
    must be discarded before steady-state periodicity holds.  May be
    omitted (treated as `0`) for memoryless seeds.

These annotations are pure metadata: the pass never mutates op operands,
types, or graph structure, and downstream passes that ignore the
attributes behave exactly as before.  The annotations are intended for
consumption by future folding passes (a planned successor to
`crag-fold-periodic-subgraphs` that can fold filter/delay chains, not
just bare oscillators) and by tooling that wants to query the
compile-time periodic structure of a graph.

**Periodicity rules implemented**

Seeds:
  * `crag.sine`, `crag.saw`, `crag.square`, `crag.tri` with `freq`,
    `phase` (and `duty`) all compile-time constant: period =
    `round(sample_rate / freq)`, transient = 0.
  * `crag.wavetable_osc`: period taken from the op's own `period`
    attribute, transient = 0.

Propagation through pure memoryless audio ops (period preserved or
combined as `lcm`, transient = `max` of inputs):
  * `crag.scale`, `crag.hard_clip`: period = input period.
  * `crag.audio_mul`: period = `lcm(p_lhs, p_rhs)`.
  * `crag.sum` (variadic): period = `lcm` over all inputs.

`crag.filter`: when the `feedback` and `feedforward` operands are
produced by the same `crag.get_filter_coeffs` op, the IIR order is
statically known.  The output period equals the input period and the
transient is `input_transient + filter_order`.

Delay lines (no-feedback case): for each `crag.delay_line` whose only
writer is one `crag.push_delay`, downstream `crag.pop_delay` and
`crag.peek_delay` get period = pushed-signal period and transient =
pushed-signal transient + `delaySize` samples.  `crag.pop_delay_mix_in`
additionally combines the dry input with `lcm` and `max(transient)`.

Feedback delay regions (period = `lcm(P, D)` per the design document):
detected when the input to the matching `crag.push_delay` transitively
depends on a read of the same delay line through linear constant-gain
ops.  The output period of the read ops becomes `lcm(P, D)` where `D`
is `delaySize`, but the transient is unbounded by this analysis and so
these ops are annotated only with `crag.period`, no `crag.transient`.

Ops whose period cannot be determined (dynamic inputs, stochastic ops
such as `crag.white_noise`, samplers, and any op not enumerated above)
are left unannotated.

This pass requires `crag-resolve-audio-rates` to have run first so that
audio types carry concrete sample-rate values.  It is a standalone
analysis: it does not need to be in the production lowering pipeline,
and is intended to be run via `crag-opt --crag-annotate-periodicity`
for inspection or as a precursor to a future folding pass.

entries.name: crag-canonicalize-graph
entries.summary: Normalizes CRAG graph attributes for deterministic execution

entries.name: crag-check-stability
entries.summary: Statically checks for known-unstable filter or delay configurations
entries.body:
Analyzes the `crag.graph` body for statically detectable instabilities:

1. **Filter instability** — if a `crag.get_filter_coeffs` op has a
   compile-time constant cutoff value, the pass computes the Butterworth
   feedback coefficients and checks whether the resulting IIR filter is
   BIBO-stable (all poles strictly inside the unit circle).  An unstable
   configuration is reported as a pass failure with a diagnostic attached
   to the offending op.

2. **Delay-line feedback gain** — if a `crag.delay_line` buffer is
   populated by a `crag.push_delay` whose input is derived from a
   `crag.pop_delay` or `crag.pop_delay_mix_in` on the *same* delay line,
   the pass checks whether any arith constant multiplier in that path
   exceeds 1.0 in magnitude.  A gain ≥ 1.0 in a pure feedback loop
   produces exponential growth and is flagged as an error.

This pass operates on the crag dialect IR and should run before any
lowering passes.

entries.name: crag-estimate-run-time
entries.summary: Estimates how long a compiled crag graph will run
entries.body:
Performs a static analysis of the graph and prints a human-readable
estimate of the total audio duration to stderr.  The estimate covers:

* **Sampler length** — `crag.sampler` handles do not carry length
  information at compile time (length is bound at runtime), so this
  component is marked as unknown unless overridden by the
  `sampler-length-samples` option.

* **Filter tail** — for a stable IIR filter of order N whose dominant
  pole has magnitude r < 1, the -60 dB decay time is
  `-60 / (20 * log10(r) * sampleRate)` seconds.  Unstable filters
  (r ≥ 1) are reported as infinite.

* **Delay tail** — a delay line contributes at most
  `delaySize / sampleRate` seconds of tail after the source signal ends,
  where `delaySize` is the stated delay reading depth (the amount of
  audio time being popped or peeked), not the full allocated buffer size
  (`maxSize`).  For modulated-delay effects that use a larger backing
  buffer (`maxSize > delaySize`), the tail estimate is still based on the
  nominal `delaySize` reading depth.

The total estimate is attached to the module as a
`crag.estimated_duration_secs` float attribute, and is also printed via
a remark diagnostic.  If any component is unknown the attribute is set
to `-1.0` (unknown).

#### Options

```
-sampler-length-samples : Assumed sampler length in samples (0 = unknown)
-sample-rate            : Sample rate override (0 = read from graph attribute)
```

entries.name: crag-infer-delay-sizes
entries.summary: Infers delay line buffer sizes for crag.delay_line ops with delaySize=0
entries.body:
Walks every `crag.graph` body and, for each `crag.delay_line` op whose
result type carries `delaySize=0`, replaces that type with a concrete
`!crag.delay<elemType, sampleRate, channels, N>` where N is at least
`block-size` samples.

The inferred size is the maximum of `block-size` (ensuring the buffer can
hold at least one full audio block) and any explicit `min-delay-size`
option.  Users who need longer delays should set the delay size explicitly
in the IR; this pass fills in a sensible compile-time default when the
user writes `delaySize=0` as a placeholder.

This pass should run after `crag-resolve-audio-rates` and before
`crag-lower-audio-to-tensor`.

#### Options

```
-block-size     : Minimum inferred delay buffer size in samples per channel
-min-delay-size : Explicit lower bound on inferred delay size (samples per channel)
```

entries.name: crag-inject-instability-check
entries.summary: Injects runtime instability checks before crag.output ops (debug pass)
entries.body:
Optional debug pass that inserts a `crag.instability_check` op before each
`crag.output` op in every `crag.graph` in the module.  The injected op
performs a per-block peak-amplitude test at runtime: if the maximum
absolute sample value in the output block exceeds `threshold` (default
2.0), the graph is flagged as unstable.

This pass must run *before* `crag-inline-subgraphs` so that the
pre-inlining graph structure is still intact.  Each injected op carries:

* `graph_name` — the name of the enclosing `crag.graph` (or `"top_level"`
  for the anonymous top-level graph).
* `param_names` — the names of all `crag.param` ops present in the
  enclosing graph before inlining.

At runtime, when instability is detected:

* `@crag_is_stable` (public i32 global) is set to 0.
* `@crag_unstable_check_idx` (public i32 global) is set to the index
  of the failing check instance.
* `@crag_instability_N_name` (public i8 array global) holds the
  null-terminated graph name for check instance N.

Both the native test host (`crag_test_host`) and the web player
(`crag_player.js`) check `@crag_is_stable` after each `crag_process()`
call and stop rendering if instability is detected, printing the graph
name and all current parameter values.

Pipeline placement: after `crag-resolve-audio-rates`, before
`crag-inline-subgraphs`.

#### Options

```
-threshold : Peak amplitude threshold above which a block is considered unstable
```
